overview.headline: Paying for college by starting with non-loan aid and comparing loan options

keyPoints.point: Students should apply for grants and scholarships before turning to federal student loans and then private loans.
keyPoints.quote: it’s generally best to apply for grants, scholarships, and then federal student loans before private loans.

keyPoints.point: Grants and scholarships are financial aid that does not have to be repaid after college.
keyPoints.quote: Grants and scholarships are a type of financial aid that doesn’t have to be repaid.

keyPoints.point: Tuition payment plans split college bills into equal monthly payments and usually do not charge interest.
keyPoints.quote: Tuition payment plans, also called tuition installment plans, are short-term payment plans that split your college bills into equal monthly payments.

keyPoints.point: Federal student loans offer fixed interest rates and income-driven repayment alternatives that private loans often lack.
keyPoints.quote: Fixed interest rates, meaning your interest rate will stay the same over time

keyPoints.point: Income share agreements require a percentage of future income and can lead to excessive debt if combined with other loans.
keyPoints.quote: Income share agreements (ISAs) are a type of private education loan where you receive money to pay for your education

keyTerms.gloss: Grants are funds for college that do not need repayment and are applied for before loans
keyTerms.quote: it’s generally best to apply for grants, scholarships, and then federal student loans before private loans.

keyTerms.gloss: Scholarships are merit-based aid that does not need repayment and can reduce borrowing
keyTerms.quote: it’s generally best to apply for grants, scholarships, and then federal student loans before private loans.

keyTerms.gloss: Tuition payment plans split college bills into short-term monthly payments without interest
keyTerms.quote: Tuition payment plans, also called tuition installment plans, are short-term payment plans that split your college bills into equal monthly payments.

keyTerms.gloss: Income share agreements require future payments based on a percentage of income until a defined amount is reached
keyTerms.quote: Income share agreements (ISAs) are a type of private education loan where you receive money to pay for your education

keyTerms.gloss: Federal student loans are made by the Department of Education with fixed rates and income-driven repayment options
keyTerms.quote: Federal student loans are made and guaranteed by the Department of Education
